content.comment_body: I am searching for a way to display a message with a timer preset, where the timer is set in one [product_name] configuration and its block is in another [product_name] setup.
Here is an example for you. Check out Parameter-VM-Mapping. Ensure the timers in both [product_name] units use the same time base.

Thank you for the response, but I still need some clarification. The timer preset for message B002 refers to the off-delay B001 in one [product_name] unit. I aim to access the B001 on-delay in another [product_name] unit. Is there something I need to adjust in my [product_name] software environment?

Using the display, you can enter the timer value in the message text for B001. The remaining time of B001 matches the timer value, and Parameter-VM-Mapping allows transferring this remaining time to the VM area. Through network connection, one [product_name] unit sends the value to another unit’s VM area. Then, in the second unit, this value can be mapped to the timer as the starting value.
Can this work in simulation, or do two actual [product_name] units on a physical network need to be used?
Simulation mode in [product_name] software doesn’t cover all functions. I have tested the proposed solution with two physical [product_name] units, version [version_no].
